correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and 0<p<=1/n the exact convolution identity, binomial mass ratio and monotone polynomial H_n establish F_t nondecreasing with F_1=(1-p)^(n-1). The Edmonds matroid-intersection argument yields an outside-good bound, and Barman--Verma MMS feasibility gives simultaneous allocations. Rank-one uniform matroids attain the upper bound; rank-t uniform matroids and Chebyshev show no positive uniform q exists for p>1/n. Equality boundaries and quantifiers checked; 3068 exact binomial and 1560 small-profile tests passed and are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023/2024 primary paper explicitly conjectures the exact p=1/n case, and the 2026 thinning paper has different all-valuation guarantees rather than the complete finite-n matroid-rank phase. The 2022 mode-based tail comparison covers a related critical-point step but not the entire subcritical probability family. The new polynomial domination argument yields a sharp continuous p-phase including the discontinuous supercritical obstruction. Overlap searches found no theorem implying the full claim; specialist literature priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The exact family Q_n(p) settles the finite-n critical value explicitly conjectured in the source, extends it over every subcritical sampling rate, and shows an abrupt collapse above the natural physical random-allocation marginal p=1/n. The phase has operational meaning as a quantile benchmark for matroid-rank resource allocation and is sharp for all n and arbitrary numbers of goods. The principal contribution is a structural classification, not a small numerical example.
